title: C# Multiple Choice Questions - Preprocessors
description: This section of our 1000+ C# MCQs focuses on preprocessors in C# Programming Language.

questions.question: Choose the symbol which begins a preprocessor directive in C#.NET?
What is meant by preprocessor directive in C#.NET?

options.text: a form of command which are interpreted by the compiler
a form of macros like in c and c++ not exactly same to them, separately designed for C#.NET
always begins with a '#' character occupies separate line of source of code

questions.explanation: Preprocessor directives are commands that are interpreted by the compiler and affect the output or behavior of the build process. The C# compiler does not have a separate preprocessor, like C and C++ we cannot use these directives to create macros. Preprocessing directives are top lines in our program that start with '#'. The '#' is followed by an identifier that is the directive name.

questions.question: What is meant by preprocessor directive #define?

options.text: helps in determining existence and non existence of a symbol
can be used to create function like macros as in C/C++

questions.explanation: The #define directive defines a character sequence called a symbol. The existence or nonexistence of a symbol can be determined by #if or #elif and is used to control compilation. #define which supports creation of function like macros in c/c++ does not support the same in C#.

questions.question: Select the defined preprocessor in C#.NET?
What does preprocessor directive #if and #endif explains?

options.text: Enables compilation of sequence of code on condition basis
Express results into true or false on evaluation of condition
If expression following #if is true then code that is between #if and #endif is compiled otherwise skipped

questions.explanation: The #if and #endif directives enable conditional compilation of a sequence of code based upon whether an expression involving one or more symbols evaluates to true. A symbol is true if it has been defined. It is false otherwise. If the expression following #if is true, the code that is between it and #endif is compiled. Otherwise, the intervening code is skipped. The #endif directive marks the end of an #if block.

questions.question: Which preprocessor directive among the following forces the compiler to stop the compilation?
questions.explanation: The #error directive forces the compiler to stop compilation. It is used for debugging. The general form of the #error directive is #error error-message. When the #error directive is encountered, the error message is displayed.

questions.question: Which among the following is not a preprocessor directive?
questions.explanation: C# preprocessor directives include #define, #undef, #if, #elif, #else, #endif, #region, #endregion, #warning, #error, #pragma, #line, and #nullable. There is no #Or. C# also has no #ifdef (use #if instead).
